claims.text: The 89th Texas Legislature passed Senate Bill 2807 in 2025. The bill created a required authorization for the commercial operation of automated vehicles on Texas roads.
claims.quote: The 89th Texas Legislature passed Senate Bill 2807 (89R) in 2025 creating a required authorization for the commercial operation of automated vehicles on Texas roads.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: The Texas Department of Motor Vehicles has the administrative authority to issue and revoke automated vehicle authorizations.
claims.quote: The Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) has administrative authority to issue and revoke these authorizations
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: On the road, enforcement belongs to the Texas Department of Public Safety and local law enforcement agencies.
claims.quote: the Texas Department of Public Safety and local law enforcement agencies have authority over on road enforcement of the operations and adherence to traffic laws
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: Senate Bill 2807 took effect on September 1st, 2025.
claims.quote: Senate Bill 2807 (89R) became effective September 1, 2025
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: From May 28th, 2026, every company operating automated vehicles commercially must hold an active authorization from the department.
claims.quote: All companies operating automated vehicles commercially on or after May 28, 2026, are required to maintain an active authorization with TxDMV.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: The department defines commercial activity as operating an automated motor vehicle to carry property or passengers for a commercial enterprise on Texas roads without a human driver.
claims.quote: Operation of an automated motor vehicle to transport property or passengers in furtherance of a commercial enterprise on Texas roads without a human driver.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: Vehicles owned by individuals and used for personal purposes need no authorization.
claims.quote: Individually owned vehicles, operated for personal use, do not require an authorization.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: The online application asks for basic contact information about the applicant.
claims.quote: The electronic application form requires basic applicant contact information.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: The applicant also acknowledges a written statement about the vehicle.
claims.quote: The applicant must also acknowledge a written statement that the vehicle is:
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: Applicants must certify that the Texas Department of Public Safety has a copy of their plan for how firefighters, police, ambulance crews and other emergency services should interact with the vehicle.
claims.quote: The applicant must also certify that the Texas Department of Public Safety has been provided a copy of the plan specifying how a person who provides firefighting, law enforcement, ambulance, medical, or other emergency services should interact with the automated motor vehicle
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: The authorization to operate automated vehicles carries no fee.
claims.quote: No fees are required for an authorization to operate automated vehicles.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: An authorization never expires. It stays valid until the department revokes it.
claims.quote: Authorizations do not expire and are valid until revoked by the department.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: An authorization holder must tell the department about any material change to its application information within 30 days.
claims.quote: An authorization holder is required to update the department of any material changes to the information provided at the time of application within 30 days of the change.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: Once approved, the authorization holder keeps its own list of active vehicles by adding and deleting the vehicles connected to its authorization.
claims.quote: the applicant will be able to maintain the listing of their active vehicles by adding and deleting specific vehicles connected to the authorization.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: From May 28th, 2026, concerns about automated vehicles operating in ways that could result in serious bodily injury or death can be sent to the department's Enforcement Division through its TxMCCS truck stop page.
claims.quote: concerns about automated vehicles operating in ways that could result in serious bodily injury or death can be submitted to the TxDMV Enforcement Division for review at https://txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: The department says it is unlikely to take administrative enforcement action in cases that fall below the serious bodily injury or death standard of Texas Penal Code Section 1.07.
claims.quote: The department is unlikely to take administrative enforcement action in cases that do not meet this standard as defined by Texas Penal Code, Section 1.07.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: The department treats an automated vehicle's operation as endangering the public when it has caused serious bodily injury or is likely to, as Texas Penal Code Section 1.07 defines it.
claims.quote: The operation of an automated motor vehicle is considered to endanger the public when the operation has resulted, or is likely to result, in serious bodily injury as defined by Section 1.07, Texas Penal Code.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: Before it takes enforcement action, the department notifies the holder and gives it a set period to correct the public safety concern.
claims.quote: provides the authorization holder a specific period of time to correct the identified public safety concern
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: When a holder appeals to the State Office of Administrative Hearings, the hearing must be held within 60 days of the department's request.
claims.quote: the hearing must be held within 60 days of the request filed by the department
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: If that hearing isn't held in time, the authorization is reinstated immediately.
claims.quote: If the hearing is not held within the required time, then the authorization is immediately reinstated.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: Law enforcement officials can check the authorization status of individual vehicles or operators on the department's TxMCCS truck stop page.
claims.quote: Law enforcement officials can verify the TxDMV AV authorization status of individual vehicles or operators at https://txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

rejected.finding: The summary report shows 3,164 vehicles authorized for commercial operation under SB 2807
rejected.reason: The report never says authorized, commercial or SB 2807. The link has to be carried by c22, c27 and c35 from the program page. The holder maintains the vehicle list itself (c35).

rejected.finding: The department is unlikely to act on complaints below serious bodily injury
rejected.reason: The page says concerns, not complaints, and the standard is serious bodily injury or death under Penal Code 1.07. c36 and c37 carry the verified wording.

rejected.finding: How the public can look up an authorization
rejected.reason: No source describes a public lookup. Only law enforcement officials verify status at the truck stop page (c42). Public access depends on Government Code Chapter 552 (c52). The deck can claim neither that the public can nor that it can't.

rejected.finding: The Volvo/Waabi and Kodiak/Charger runs operate under the authorizations listed in the report
rejected.reason: No source makes the link. Neither release mentions a TxDMV authorization, and the report lists no routes. The rows (c7, c15) and the corporate statements (c62 to c67) stay separate facts.

rejected.finding: An observer or a safety driver is or isn't a human driver under Transportation Code 545.451
rejected.reason: No source applies the definition to these operations. Deciding it would be an inference.

rejected.finding: Atlas Energy Solutions' 38 listed vehicles are Kodiak driverless trucks in the Permian
rejected.reason: Kodiak names Atlas as a customer, but no source says the 38 are Kodiak-equipped trucks.
